title: I Followed the Museum Bag Policy Into the Gift Shop

parts.text: I checked my backpack at 10:02 because the sign said bags larger than a sheet of paper had to be free of the galleries. The attendant, Rhonda, waved me through with a smile that did not reach the lockers. Inside, a man with a hiking pack was taking flash photos of a textile. I told a guard. The guard said Rhonda makes exceptions for members. I was not a member. I was thirty-three with a timed ticket. I asked to retrieve my bag to buy the member line just to be in the same policy. Rhonda said retrieval was a re-entry fee. I photographed the sign, the hiking pack, and the re-entry price. Then the textile alarm went off because the hiking pack had brushed the case.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The member exception just set off the textile alarm.

social.video_title: They made me check a bag a member wore into the gallery — Part 1/2
social.description: Timed ticket, lockers, and a hiking pack in front of a textile. Re-entry cost extra. Would you have said something to the guard?

parts.text: Security pulled the member aside. The policy was for everyone. Rhonda's exceptions were not in the manual. They refunded my locker fee and waived re-entry. I walked the galleries with a small tote they sold me at cost, which is still money, but it was on the sign. The hiking pack went back to the coat check. The textile kept existing. I bought a postcard of it and did not flash. Rhonda checked the next bags with a ruler. The ruler had been in a drawer the whole time. I used my timed ticket until it expired like a normal person.

social.video_title: The ruler had been in the drawer the whole time — Part 2/2
social.description: Alarms, a manual without exceptions, and a locker refund. Was membership a hiking pass?
